withdrawn_independence_estimate.note: Not a lower bound. The finished 3,810,409-byte archive is 122,709 B smaller, because the independence model gives no credit for cross-genome sharing.

verdict_basis: The measured anchor channel alone is 2,257,234 B (1.88x the target) and would need 1.018 bits/base, 1.77x better than the best DNA rate measured here. Independently, the measured non-anchor channels alone are 1,553,175 B (1.29x the target). Both components exceed the whole budget. This is measured evidence, not an information-theoretic proof.
assumptions: The channel bytes are the measured ArchiveByteAccounting decomposition of the finished tuned archive and sum exactly to 3,810,409 B.
The best measured DNA rate is QCRM at 1.806 bits/base on a single 5.07 Mbp E. coli genome; JARVIS3 reaches 2.035 bits/base on this anchor, and the finished archive reaches 1.914 bits/base on it.
The anchor bank (9,434,480 bases) is the distinct non-redundant content of the 24 genomes; any faithful archive must convey it or a reference plus the same amount of variation.
A radically different generative representation could in principle beat these measured bounds, but no measured method is close.
